items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The guard `if not self.field.is_cached(rel_obj):` (and the matching `remote_field.is_cached` / `self.related.field.is_cached` guards) says what it does. The formatting matches the surrounding code. There is no new comment explaining why the guard exists, which is a minor gap.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: It reuses the existing field cache API (`is_cached`) and adds no new bookkeeping. It applies the same two-line guard in the three parallel `get_prefetch_queryset` loops, which follows the existing per-descriptor structure. No dead code or debug output is left behind.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: The change is a small conditional with no exception handling and no magic constants. When the relation isn't cached, the existing behaviour is kept. It passed all 85 hidden pass-to-pass tests and the agent's own run across 11 test modules.

items.name: Guard is conditional and covers the one-to-one variant
items.name_zh: 仅在已缓存时跳过回填，并考虑一对一情形
items.evidence: The reverse-FK path is guarded with `if not self.field.is_cached(rel_obj):`. `ReverseOneToOneDescriptor` (`if not self.related.field.is_cached(rel_obj)`) and `ForwardManyToOneDescriptor` are guarded the same way. If the relation isn't cached, the parent is still assigned, so a plain prefetch doesn't trigger extra queries.
